steps.label: Do Now: Follow the Sequence
steps.content:
Do Now: Follow the Sequence

An algorithm is an ordered set of instructions. Cambridge pseudocode is a structured way to write those instructions. A sequence runs one line at a time from top to bottom.

Quick reference

<- stores the value on the right in the variable on the left.

OUTPUT displays a value.

1  Number <- 4
2  Number <- Number + 2
3  OUTPUT Number

Questions

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Three Pseudocode Instructions
steps.content:
Three Pseudocode Instructions

Read each instruction exactly. The keyword or assignment arrow tells the computer what to do.

steps.label: Worked Trace Table
steps.content:
Worked Trace Table

For this run, the user enters 5. Record a new row only when an instruction runs. Only fill in a cell when that line changes it, or when that line is the one that outputs it, otherwise leave the cell blank.

steps.label: Trace Table Walkthrough
steps.content:
Trace Table Walkthrough

Complete a guided sequence before working independently.

Steps

  1. Open Trace Tables.
  2. At the top of the page, select Cambridge pseudocode.
  3. Open Walkthrough and choose Sequence.
  4. Predict what the program will output.
  5. Select Next Step until all four lines have been traced.

Complete when: the table contains four completed rows and the final row contains the program output.

steps.label: Turn Instructions into Pseudocode
steps.content:
Turn Instructions into Pseudocode

The task is to receive a length and a width, calculate the area, then display the area.

steps.label: Write It Yourself
steps.content:
Write It Yourself

Use the same structure you just learned, but write it yourself this time.

Task

Write pseudocode for an algorithm that:

  • asks for the Price
  • asks for the Quantity
  • works out the Total
  • displays the Total

Remember

  • Every line runs in order, top to bottom.
  • Use INPUT to receive a value.
  • Use <- to work something out and store it.
  • Use OUTPUT to display a value.

steps.label: Independent Trace Table Practice
steps.content:
Independent Trace Table Practice

Use each line of code to decide which trace table cell changes.

Required work

  1. Select Cambridge pseudocode.
  2. Open Practice, choose Sequence, and complete Sequence Foundations.
  3. Use Check Answers. Correct your table until it shows Perfect.
  4. Open the Auto-Generator, choose Sequence and Easy.
  5. Complete one generated question correctly.

Complete when: Sequence Foundations shows Perfect and one generated Sequence question has been answered correctly. Progress is saved to your account.

steps.label: Create Your Profile
steps.content:
Create Your Profile

A variable is a named place where a program stores a value. Use assignment to store five values about yourself.

Variables to create

  • Name, text inside quotation marks
  • Age, a number
  • FavouriteColour, text inside quotation marks
  • Hobby, text inside quotation marks
  • FavouriteFood, text inside quotation marks

Write one assignment for each variable. The instructions can be in any order.

Name <- "Amina"
Age <- 12

steps.label: Plenary
steps.content:
Plenary

Use everything from today. Try this on your own before checking your answer.

Task

Write pseudocode for an algorithm that:

  • asks for the number of Tickets
  • asks for the PricePerTicket
  • works out the Cost
  • displays the Cost

Remember

  • Every line runs in order, top to bottom.
  • Use INPUT to receive a value.
  • Use <- to work something out and store it.
  • Use OUTPUT to display a value.

lines.feedback: Line 3 must calculate Price * Quantity and assign the result to Total using <-.
Line 3 must calculate Tickets * PricePerTicket and assign the result to Cost using <-.
